newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - LCI sees adding 8 local markets.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - LCI sees adding 8 local markets.

text.p: LCI International's top executive said Thursday he hopes to have the long-distance provider competing for local telephone service in 30 domestic markets by the year's end.

Chairman and chief executive officer H. Brian Thompson told Reuters in an interview that LCI is close to completing an agreement with Bell Atlantic Corp to add another eight local service areas to the 22 markets in 10 states it now serves.
LCI has regulatory authority to provide local service on a resale basis in 26 states and the District of Columbia and it has applications pending in another 14.
LCI's local service is offered only to commercial -- not residential -- customers.

The move to provide local service should pose no threat to the company's operating margin -- among the industry's highest -- even as similar efforts have proven to be tremendously costly to such competitors as MCI Communications Corp, Thompson said.

The company is protecting its margin during the move by steering clear of the temptation to build its own local facilities to circumvent the Baby Bell systems already in place. MCI, on the other hand, is investing hundreds of millions of dollars to build its own network and its earnings and margins are taking a beating as a result.
Thompson said LCI's margins should remain in the 18-to-20 percent range for the forseeable future.

LCI has managed to keep its profit margin high through its strategy of buying fiber optic network capacity rather than leasing it. It struck a $100 million deal earlier this year with IXC Communications Inc to acquire a position on a fiber optic line being built from Chicago to Los Angeles.
The high margin makes it less vulnerable to pricing pressures, according to analysts reports.

Looking forward at earnings, Thompson said that, unless the company is involved in a second half acquisition, which is always a possibility, "I see no reaon why we shouldn't" match Wall Street's estimates, given the momentum LCI is carrying out of the just-finished second quarter.
Late Wednesday, LCI reported its 23rd straight quarter of earnings growth.
Revenue, operating income and net income growth rates all were up 20 percent or more from a year ago.
Revenues for the quarter grew 26 percent to $338.4 million from $269.4 million a year ago.

Net income was up 21 percent to $21.4 million, or $0.25 per share, versus $17.7 million, or $0.20 per share ($0.19 fully taxed), in 1996. Operating income grew 23 percent to $42.6 million against $34.7 million last year.

MacLean, Va.-based LCI, which is classed as a second-tier long distance provider behind the Big Three -- AT&T Corp, MCI Communications Corp and Sprint Corp -- experienced gains across its main services -- residential, business and international long-distance, plus local service.
Thompson said he expects balanced growth to continue.

LCI also continues to show strong growth in average minutes of use along its long-distance network. In the second quarter, minutes of use grew 39 percent from a year ago and Thompson said he sees no slowing in that trend.
"I'm quite bullish about where we are and where we are headed," he said.
